learn.title: Smart Grids: Digitizing the Power System
learn.intro: Smart grids use digital communication to balance electricity supply and demand in real time. They enable two-way energy flows, support renewable integration, and reduce outage times. As solar and wind grow, smart grids become essential for a resilient, efficient, and low-carbon energy future worldwide.
learn.c1_text: Smart grids monitor electricity flow like air traffic control tracks planes. Advanced sensors called phasor measurement units (PMUs) collect data every few milliseconds. This lets operators see grid conditions instantly and respond before small issues become blackouts.
learn.c2_text: Unlike traditional one-way grids, smart grids allow homes with rooftop solar to sell excess power back. Smart meters track usage in 15-minute intervals instead of monthly. This flexibility helps balance variable renewables and empowers consumers as 'prosumers'.
learn.c3_text: India launched the Smart Grid Mission in 2013 with plans to install 130 million smart meters by 2025. States like Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu are piloting smart metering projects. These efforts aim to cut distribution losses from 20% to under 12% and integrate 500 GW renewables by 2030.
learn.stat1: Over 70 countries are implementing smart grid technologies as of 2023
learn.stat2: Smart meters reduce billing errors by up to 90% compared to manual readings
learn.stat3: India aims to deploy 130 million smart meters by 2025 under its Smart Grid Mission
learn.stat4: Grid digitization can improve operational efficiency by 15-20% according to IEA estimates

learn.title: Carbon Markets and Clean Energy Incentives
learn.intro: Carbon markets put a price on pollution, making clean energy more competitive. Companies buy allowances or credits to offset emissions, funding renewable projects. This market-driven approach mobilizes private capital for decarbonization and helps countries meet climate targets efficiently.
learn.c1_text: Cap-and-trade sets a limit on total emissions and issues tradable permits. Companies that emit less can sell extra allowances. The EU ETS, launched in 2005, covers 40% of EU emissions. Prices reached €100 per ton in 2023, incentivizing rapid clean energy adoption.
learn.c2_text: Carbon credits represent one tonne of CO2 reduced or removed. Projects like wind farms or forest conservation earn credits sold to polluters. Each credit should represent real, measurable, and verifiable emission reductions verified by third parties under approved standards.
learn.c3_text: India's Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme covers 1,400 industries. It saved 11.5 million tonnes CO2 in cycle I (2016-19). The scheme rewards energy efficiency improvements with tradable certificates, helping industries cut costs while meeting national climate commitments.
learn.stat1: Global carbon markets reached $2.5 trillion in value in 2023
learn.stat2: The EU ETS generated €200 billion in carbon revenue since 2005
learn.stat3: India's PAT scheme saved 11.5 million tonnes of CO2 in its first cycle
learn.stat4: Voluntary carbon markets transacted 200 million credits worth $2 billion in 2022

learn.title: Lithium-Ion Battery Storage Explained
learn.intro: Lithium-ion batteries store excess renewable energy for use when the sun isn't shining or wind isn't blowing. They enable grid stability, support electric vehicles, and make clean energy reliable. As costs fall, battery storage becomes key to transitioning away from fossil fuels globally.
learn.c1_text: Lithium ions move between anode and cathode through electrolyte. Charging forces ions to the anode; discharging moves them back, creating electron flow. Like a sponge soaking up water, the battery stores chemical energy that releases as electricity when needed.
learn.c2_text: Large battery farms provide frequency regulation within seconds. Tesla's Hornsdale Power Reserve in Australia responds in 140 milliseconds. These systems prevent blackouts, store surplus solar, and defer costly grid upgrades. A single utility-scale battery can power 50,000 homes for hours.
learn.c3_text: India plans 4-hour battery storage mandatory for new renewable projects above 50 MW. The Production Linked Incentive scheme allocates $2.6 billion for domestic battery cell manufacturing. NTPC's 850 MWh battery project in Gujarat demonstrates grid-scale storage potential.
learn.stat1: Lithium-ion battery prices fell 89% from 2010 to 2022
learn.stat2: Tesla's Hornsdale Power Reserve responds to grid events in 140 milliseconds
learn.stat3: India allocated $2.6 billion for battery manufacturing under its PLI scheme
learn.stat4: Global grid-scale battery deployments reached 12 GWh in 2022

learn.title: India's National Green Hydrogen Mission
learn.intro: India's National Green Hydrogen Mission aims to make the country a global hub for clean hydrogen production. With ambitious targets and financial incentives, it seeks to decarbonize heavy industries and transportation. This initiative positions India at the forefront of the emerging hydrogen economy.
learn.c1_text: Green hydrogen will replace fossil fuels in steel, cement, and fertilizer production. Indian Oil plans to blend 10% hydrogen in refinery operations. Ports and steel plants in Gujarat and Odisha are early adopters. Export potential includes supplying Japan and Europe.
learn.stat1: India targets 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen production by 2030

learn.title: Solar PV Panels and the Photoelectric Effect
learn.intro: Solar photovoltaic panels convert sunlight directly into electricity using the photoelectric effect. When photons hit semiconductor materials, they knock electrons loose, generating current. This clean technology powers homes, businesses, and grids worldwide, reducing reliance on fossil fuels.
learn.c1_text: India has 90 GW of solar capacity installed by 2024. The Bhadla Solar Park in Rajasthan spans 14,000 acres with 2,200 MW capacity. Rooftop solar schemes target 40 GW by 2030. State policies like net metering in Gujarat encourage distributed solar adoption.

learn.title: Concentrated Solar Power Technology
learn.intro: Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) uses mirrors to focus sunlight onto a receiver, generating heat that drives turbines. Unlike PV panels, CSP can store thermal energy for hours, providing dispatchable clean power even after sunset. This makes CSP valuable for 24/7 renewable energy systems.
learn.c1_text: India's National Solar Mission includes 20,000 MW CSP targets. Rajasthan's 125 MW CSP plant at Jodhpur uses molten salt storage. The country receives over 300 sunny days annually. CSTEP's research focuses on hybrid PV-CSP systems for improved land use efficiency.

learn.stat2: CSP plants can store thermal energy for 10-15 hours after sunset
